sourceFacts: The cab has a 7-inch high-resolution multifunction monitor and a multifunction controller.
The controller selects and adjusts menu items including maintenance support, attachment flow and optional rear-view monitor functions.

sourceFacts.fact: The monitor is not a single picture: the manual enumerates six menus, thirteen submenus, and sixteen fields on the basic screen.
ACC/ON starts a roughly two-second startup state; ACC shows hour, clock and radio, while ON enters the basic screen; the alternator alarm persists until generation begins.
The optional password flow has a three-failure buzzer state and configurable validity duration.
Alarm List exists in the main menu only when a current alarm exists and lists only current alarms.
Auto Shut-Down has a timed warning, buzzer phases, idle reduction, stop transition and a pilot-lever abort condition.
Rear-view camera monitoring is optional; when enabled its image is continuously shown on the basic screen and remains only an aid.
With rear camera off, the under-meter area can be OFF, Logo or Operation Information.
Information contains Operation, Maintenance and Monitoring with resettable hours, maintenance notice/interval behavior and engine-speed monitoring.
The physical switch panel defines controller actions and state-changing switches; ECO is the engine-start default and work lights cause night mode.
Return-previous, return-basic and selector-knob input types are distinct: selector push opens/confirms while rotate moves the cursor.
Brightness adjustment requires an ordered selector path; clockwise brightens and counterclockwise darkens; day and night brightness are independently adjustable.
Work-light position 2 enters monitor night mode with the night mark; numeric key 0 can activate the daytime screen while lights remain on.
The selected passage does not explicitly bind monitor mode for work-light position 1 or OFF; those transitions remain UNKNOWN rather than inferred.

externalTeacher.explicitNoveltyAnswer: It knows how to bind a qualifying input to a PerformanceEventTiming entry and separate input delay, event-processing duration and presentation delay until the next rendering update; KAOPU N322 only knew the expected control effect and final screen.
provenance: W3C Working Draft, Event Timing API, 13 November 2026
externalTeacher.maintenance: ACTIVE; W3C draft published 2026-11-13 and repository commit a2f18d7 on 2026-11-13.
externalTeacher.runnableEvidence: WPT event-timing tests and event-timing-test-utils.js provide cross-browser executable checks for ordering, duration thresholds and interaction identifiers.
externalTeacher.licenseAndRights: Specification documents use the W3C Document License; WPT code uses BSD-3-Clause. No model assets or training data are required.
externalTeacher.directRelevance: Directly measures browser input-to-next-paint latency for the standalone HTML monitor interaction that the user reports as slow.
externalTeacher.addedKnowledge: Standard timestamp semantics, interactionId grouping, next-paint duration, and first-input capture.
integrationRisk: Event Timing duration is rounded to 8 ms.
Future entries can use durationThreshold down to 16 ms, but the default buffered threshold is 104 ms.
Browser support and device performance must be recorded; fixture timings cannot substitute for the user's physical device.
The 104 ms exposure default and general INP guidance are not KAOPU acceptance thresholds.
externalTeacher.demoOrClosureRisk: Not demo-only: normative processing model plus WPT tests exist. It is still a Working Draft and may change; no production adoption until a Mother replay proves compatibility.

metricSemantics.presentationDelayMs: max(0, startTime + duration - processingEnd), allowing documented 8 ms duration coarsening
metricSemantics.totalInteractionLatencyMs: duration, from input timestamp to the next rendering update after dispatch
metricSemantics.measurementSeparation: COLD_READY and WARM_READY samples must not share one aggregation.

thresholdPolicy.rule: Neither W3C exposure defaults nor generic INP guidance may be silently promoted into a KAOPU pass threshold. Until a threshold is frozen by the relevant Mother/user contract, measurements may diagnose but may not claim latency PASS.
